title: DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident"
content_md: DreamHost has forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users following an incident that disrupted connections to the File Manager interface. The latest update from the web hosting provider notes that all affected account owners have received recovery instructions. Users will be unable to log in until their account owner sets new credentials. DreamHost is a U.S. web hosting provider and domain registrar that offers WordPress hosting, business email, virtual private servers, dedicated servers, and cloud services. According to the company page, it serves over 400,000 customers in more than 100 countries and supports at least 1.5 million websites and applications, including 750,000 WordPress installations. DreamHost initially reported connectivity problems affecting its File Manager interface on October 23, but the impact quickly expanded to other services. The company responded by blocking access to all users until they completed password resets, an action described as a precaution. Over the weekend, the company sent out recovery instructions in batches and notified all affected account holders. As of publishing, the incident remains active and access to File Manager is still unavailable. In notifications to impacted account holders , the company advises users to also review each email address for forwarding rules and remove any forwarding destination they do not recognize.
